results.evidence_text: The subjects were 49,920 men aged 40-69 years who completed a questionnaire that included their green tea consumption habit at baseline and were followed until the end of 2004. During this time, 404 men were newly diagnosed with prostate cancer
results.one_sentence_explanation: Title, abstract, and MeSH describe an original prospective cohort evaluating green tea consumption and incident prostate cancer, and nothing in the allowed evidence establishes duplication, so the Claude+Gemini INCLUDE decision is supported over ChatGPT's S2-DUPLICATE exclusion.
